newsitem.title: BELGIUM: S&P upgrades CCB rating outlook to stable.
newsitem.headline: S&P upgrades CCB rating outlook to stable.

text.p: Credit agency Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had revised up its rating outlook for Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet, Belgium's second largest bank, to stable from negative.
"At the same time, the AA+ long-term credit rating and the A-1+ short-term credit rating of CCB have been affirmed," S&P said in a statement.
"The change in outlook reflects the improving financial performance of CCB," it added.

Standard & Poor's said it viewed CCB's cross-border alliance with French local authority lender Credit Local de France as positive for the bank, increasing its market reach and adding geographical diversity.

Standard & Poor's said while competition in the Belgian banking sector will continue to pressure the bank's net interest margin, it expected operating profitability to hold steady as CCB continues to grow outside its core business of lending to local authorities.

"If net interest margins continue to decrease, or if the bank's risk profile deteriorated significantly, CCB's long-term rating could come under downward pressure. Standard & Poor's discounts these possibilities, however, and thus the rating's outlook is stable," S&P said.

S&P's statement was made one day after its French unit S&P-ADEF said it had lowered its rating on the long-term debt of French bank Credit Local de France and its subsidiaries to AA+ from AAA but modified its outlook on the bank's long-term paper to stable from negative.
